data.name: OverviewDescription
data.value: Monitor your Kubernetes resources in one place.

data.value: No cluster connected. Select a context in Settings to get started.

data.name: GetStartedDescription
data.value: Configure a Kubernetes connection to explore cluster resources, including Pods, on the Resources page. Changes are confirmed before they are sent to the cluster.

data.name: ResourcesDescription
data.value: Browse the resource types advertised by the cluster and inspect objects in the selected namespace.

data.name: ConnectFromSettings
data.value: Configure and connect a profile in Settings. Then select a cluster and namespace at the bottom of the navigation sidebar.

data.name: NoObjectsForFilter
data.value: No objects found for this type and filter.

data.name: WikiDescription
data.value: Fundamentals for understanding the objects shown in the visualizer.

data.name: PodDescription
data.value: A Pod is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes. It groups one or more containers that share networking and volumes.

data.name: DeploymentDescription
data.value: A Deployment describes the desired number and version of Pods and coordinates updates and replacements.

data.name: ServiceDescription
data.value: A Service provides a stable address for reaching a set of Pods selected by labels.

data.name: ConfigMapDescription
data.value: A ConfigMap stores non-sensitive configuration data that can be mounted as files or environment variables.

data.name: NotFoundDescription
data.value: The requested address does not match a page in this application.

data.name: SettingsDescription
data.value: Manage Kubernetes connections and connect the clusters used by the visualizer.

data.name: ConnectionStorageDescription
data.value: Add as many connections as you need. Profiles are stored in SQLite; only the name, kubeconfig path, and context are saved. Credentials remain in the Kubernetes file.

data.name: RelatedLabelsDescription
data.value: Resources with the same key and value are grouped in the graph. The default label visualizer.k8s.io/related-set is always enabled; additional labels are saved in SQLite.

data.name: NoConnectionsYet

data.name: WikiService

data.name: DashboardAutoGeneratedResourcesTooltip
data.value: Hides Events, Endpoints, EndpointSlices, IPAddress, Leases, metrics, ComponentStatus, ControllerRevision, VolumeAttachment, and other cluster-generated support resources, plus the kubernetes Service in the default namespace. Turn it off to include them in the graph.

data.name: DashboardSystemResourcesTooltip
data.value: Hides resources in kube-system, kube-public, and kube-node-lease, resources marked as Kubernetes-created, and cluster infrastructure kinds such as APIService, ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding, FlowSchema, webhooks, and CRDs.

data.name: DashboardControllerManagedTooltip
data.value: Hides resources that declare at least one ownerReference. The owning/controller resource remains visible.

data.name: DashboardStandaloneTooltip
data.value: Hides resources without any ownerReference. If an object declares an ownerReference whose target is not loaded, it is still treated as having an owner.

data.name: ResourceOriginFilterNote
data.value: Origin is estimated from system namespaces, managedFields, and ownerReferences; Kubernetes has no universal marker for “user” versus “system” resources.

data.name: SecretYamlRedacted
data.value: For safety, YAML shows Secret metadata only; data and stringData are not loaded.

data.name: ClipboardUnavailable

data.name: WikiHeroDescription
data.value: A practical guide to the API, objects, relationships, scheduling, and cluster operations.

data.name: PodControlNote
data.value: Kubernetes has no pause operation for a Pod. Deleting it may cause its controller to create another one; to stop the workload, scale its owning Deployment, StatefulSet, or ReplicaSet to zero.
